q: 1. A plumb bob is required .............
options: when measuring distances along slopes in a hilly country
for accurate centering of a theodolite over a station mark
for testing the vertically of ranging poles
explain: A plumb bob is an essential tool for transferring points vertically, centering instruments, and ensuring verticality.

q: 2. In a traverse, the algebraic sum of the deflection angles, taking the right hand deflection angles as positive and left hand deflection as negative, should be equal to
explain: In a closed traverse, the sum of the deflection angles must equal 360° to return to the original direction.

q: 3. A traverse consists of six side, then the sum of external angle must be
explain: The sum of exterior angles is (2N + 4) × 90°. For N=6, (12 + 4) × 90 = 16 × 90 = 1440°.

q: 4. In closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: As noted in Q332, the total turn required to close a loop is a full circle (360°).

q: 5. In a closed traverse, the closing error should not be more than
explain: Errors in angles tend to accumulate in proportion to the square root of the number of stations (√N).

q: 6. The angular and linear measurement of the part of the traverse can be checked by
explain: Cut-off lines and observations to distant known objects are common ways to verify accuracy within a large traverse.

q: 7. The distance between terminal points computed from a subsidiary traverse run between them is known as
explain: A traverse base refers to the line connecting the start and end points of a traverse segment.

q: 8. The maximum number of omitted measurements that can be calculated from latitudes and departures of a closed traverse is
explain: Since there are two independent equations (ΣL=0 and ΣD=0), you can solve for a maximum of two unknowns (e.g., one length and one bearing).

q: 9. Axis method of traverse correction is used when
options: the angles are measured very accurately
the lengths are measured very accurately
both (a) and (b) are not measured very accurately
explain: The Axis method is specialized for cases where angular precision far exceeds linear precision.

q: 10. If the sum of northing of a traverse exceeds the sum of southing by 2m and sum of easting exceeds the sum of westing by 2m, the resulting closing error will be
explain: Error = √(ΣL² + ΣD²) = √(2² + 2²) = √8 = 2√2 m.

q: 11. The perpendicular distance of the mid point of the line from the reference meridian is known as
explain: Meridian distance of a line is the distance of its midpoint from the reference meridian.

q: 12. Right face and left face reading are taken to
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: While it also helps with collimation (Q319), the provided answer specifically highlights the trunnion (horizontal) axis error.

q: 13. The deflection angle may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read ............ on back station.
explain: By zeroing the theodolite on the back station and then transiting the telescope and turning to the next station, the deflection angle can be read directly.

q: 14. The direct angles may have any value between
explain: Direct angles (angles to the right) are measured clockwise from the back station to the forward station and can range anywhere from 0° to 360°.

q: 15. The line of sight is kept as high above ground surface as possible to minimize the error in the observed angles due to
explain: Air layers near the ground are more turbulent and dense, causing light to bend (refraction) and vibrate (shimmering). Raising the line of sight passes the light through more stable air.

q: 16. The distance between terminal points computed from known, as
explain: A traverse base is a line whose length and direction are precisely known or calculated to serve as a reference for the rest of the survey network.

q: 17. To avoid large centering error with very short legs, observations are generally made
options: to a target fixed on theodolite tripod
explain: When traverse legs are short, even a small displacement in centering causes a large angular error. Using high-precision optical plummet systems and fixed targets minimizes this risk.

q: 18. For removing the parallax
options: image brought in plane of cross-hairs...
explain: Parallax is eliminated by first focusing the eyepiece for the observer's eye and then focusing the objective to ensure the image falls exactly on the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 19. The capacity of a telescope of producing a sharp image is called its
explain: Definition (or resolving power) refers to the clarity and sharpness of the image produced by the telescope's lenses.

q: 20. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse .............
options: exterior angles are measures when the traverse goes anti-clockwise
explain: In a closed traverse, running counter-clockwise results in the measurement of interior angles when observing angles to the right.

q: 21. When the first object is to be focused, the scale is set to 0° 00' 00'' and then .............
options: the upper screw is fixed, lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, top tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient
explain: To keep the initial reading at zero while sighting the first station, the upper plate must be locked to the lower plate (reading 0), and the whole instrument rotated using the lower clamp/tangent screws.

q: 22. For a closed traverse the omitted measurements may be calculated .............
options: length or bearing of adjacent side
explain: In a closed traverse, if $\sum Latitude = 0$ and $\sum Departure = 0$, you can solve for up to two unknown quantities (like one length and one bearing, or two lengths).

q: 23. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by .............
explain: All three formulas are mathematically valid based on the geometry of coordinates and bearings ($Lat = L \cos \theta$, $Dep = L \sin \theta$).

q: 24. The deflection angle may have any value between .............
explain: A deflection angle is the angle between a survey line and the prolongation of the preceding line. It can theoretically range from 0 (straight line) to 180 degrees (reversal).

q: 25. While rotating the theodolite in the horizontal plane, the bubble of the bubble tube takes up the same position in its tube, it indicates .............
options: the line of collimation is perpendicular to vertical axis
explain: If the bubble remains centered throughout a 360-degree rotation, it confirms the vertical axis of the instrument is truly vertical.

q: 26. You have to observe an included angle with better accuracy than what is achievable by a vernier, you will prefer the method of .............
explain: The method of repetition allows the same angle to be measured multiple times and divided by the number of repetitions, which reduces the least-count error.

q: 27. Centering error of a theodolite produces an error .............
options: which does not vary with the direction or pointing
which varies with the direction of pointing and inversely with the length of sight
explain: The effect of centering error is more significant on short sights than on long sights.

q: 28. In horizontal angles, the error due to imperfect leveling of the plate bubble is .............
options: large when sights are nearly level
explain: If the instrument is not level, the horizontal axis is not horizontal; this error is magnified significantly when the telescope is tilted steeply upward or downward.

q: 29. Which of the following errors can be eliminated by taking mean of both face observations?
options: errors due to eccentricity of verniers
errors due to imperfect adjustments of plate levels
errors due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to horizontal axis
explain: Taking the average of Face Left and Face Right readings eliminates instrumental errors such as the horizontal axis not being perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 30. An angle between the inclined line of sight and the horizontal is called .............
explain: Vertical angles are measured in the vertical plane between the horizontal line of sight and the target line.

q: 31. Can the vertical axis coincide with any other axis in any position of telescope?
options: Yes, with the geometric centre of level head
Yes, with the axis of altitude levels
explain: In specific adjustment positions, the vertical axis can align with the axis of the altitude bubble tube to ensure horizontal rotation.

q: 32. For a transit theodolite the least reading on the main scale is 20'. If its vernier scale should read 20", then .............
options: 59° on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20° on the main scale are divided into 60 equal divisions
19° 40' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20° 20' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
explain: For a least count of 20", the vernier must divide $(n-1)$ divisions of the main scale. Here, 59 divisions of 20' each ($19° 40'$) are divided into 60 parts on the vernier.
